newsitem.title: USA: BankAmerica, First Chicago report higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: BankAmerica, First Chicago report higher earnings.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp. and First Chicago NBD Corp., two of the nation's largest banks, reported higher fourth-quarter earnings Wednesday.
Fleet Financial Group Inc. and Wachovia Corp. also reported higher earnings.
San Francisco-based BankAmerica said it earned $747 million in the fourth quarter, up from $704 million a year earlier.
BankAmerica said the earnings equalled $1.93 a share, up from $1.74 in the 1995 quarter and better than Wall Street analysts' projections of $1.90 a share for the latest quarter.
BankAmerica, the nation's third largest banking company, was up $3.25 at $105 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Its assets increased to $250.8 billion from $232.5 a year earlier.
Net interest income fell to $2.13 billion from $2.15 billion and non-interest income increased to $1.5 billion from $1.16 billion. Trading income grew to $134 million from $115 million.

Michael O'Neill, chief financial officer, said in a conference call with reporters that the company's domestic loans grew by $3 billion to $139 billion during the quarter, with loans in California accounting for about 30 percent of the gain.
For the year, BankAmerica earned $2.9 billion, or $7.31 a share, up from $2.7 billion, or $6.49 a share, in 1995.

First Chicago, the nation's ninth largest banking company with assets of $104.6 billion, said it earned $377 million in the fourth quarter, up from $318 million in the 1995 period. Its assets a year earlier were $122 billion.
First Chicago, parent company of First National Bank of Chicago and other banks in Indiana and Florida, said it earned $1.14 a share, up from 96 cents a share a year earlier.
For the year, First Chicago earned a record $1.44 billion, or $4.32 a share. A year earlier, the company earned $1.34 billion, or $3.99 a share.
"Our record earnings exemplify the successful first year of First Chicago NBD," said Chairman Verne Istock. "We met all of our merger-related goals on or ahead of schedule."
The company said operating expenses for 1996 edged lower, while its credit card business produced record profits for the fourth quarter.
Trading profits were $12 million in the quarter, compared with a $12 million loss in the third quarter.
First Chicago stock added $1.375 to $55.50, also on the NYSE.
Fleet Financial, the nation's 11th largest banking company, said it earned $302 million, or $1.05 a share, up from $260 million, or 94 cents a share, a year earlier.
Boston-based Fleet was up 37.5 cents a share at $52.625 in afternoon trading on the NYSE.
Wachovia Corp., said it earned $171 million, or $1.02 a share, in the fourth quarter, up from $146.2 millionm or 85 cents a share, a year earlier.
For the year, Wachovia earned $644.6 million, or $3.80 a share, up from $602.5 million, or $3.49 a share, a year earlier.
Gains in both periods reflected increases in net interest income and lower expenses, said L. M. Baker Jr., chief executive officer.

Wachovia, which is based in Winston-Salem, N.C., and operates banks in the Carolinas and Georgia, ranks as the nation's 20th largest banking company. The company's stock was off 62.5 cents at $56.25 on the NYSE.
